newsitem.title: ITALY: BASKETBALL-OLYMPIAKOS AND BARCELONA LINE UP A CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-OLYMPIAKOS AND BARCELONA LINE UP A CLASSIC.

text.p: The basketball final most people wanted but few could have confidently forecast three months ago -- Olympiakos against Barcelona -- comes true on Thursday.

In January, the glamour sides of European basketball were struggling in the EuroLeague qualifying, Olympiakos ending their first 16 games with a modest 9-7 record while Barcelona were even worse at 8-8.
But the Greek club, hit by injuries, battled to the quarter-finals where they beat their biggest rivals of all, Panathinaikos, to claim their Final Four ticket.

Barcelona, galvanised by the arrival from TeamSystem Bologna of Serb Sasha Djordjevic, rallied to make the last eight and then edge aside Bologna to book their sixth Final Four outing in the last nine years.

On Tuesday, both clubs made their experience of the big time count, defeating opponents making their first Final Four appearances. Olympiakos overcame Ljubljana from Slovenia 75-64 and Barcelona ousted Villeurbanne of France 77-70.
Losing coaches agreed. Villeurbanne's Greg Beugnot said: "Our major problem was experience. We could not get control of the game when it was necessary."
Zmago Sagadin of Ljubljana echoed: "Olympiakos are a more experienced team and this was obvious at the most important moments."
It all means that at long last, after a combined total of five losing appearances in finals, one of the continent's great clubs will lift the crown.

They have both been there -- and not quite done it. Olympiakos lost in 1994 and 1995 and Barcelona most recently in 1996 when they were beaten by just one point by Panathinaikos in controversial circumstances.
So whose heartache will end on Thursday night when the two sides line up in the white-hot atmosphere engendered by a capacity 10,800 crowd in Rome's Palaeur arena?
Olympiakos are at full strength and if ex-Los Angeles Lakers playmaker David Rivers, top-scorer on Tuesday with 28 points, can work his magic they will be more than halfway there.
But if Djordjevic can dominate as he did for noticeable spells against Villeurbanne it could be a different story.
Maybe the fans will sway it. The 5,500 Olympiakos supporters, festooned in red and white, make enough noise to all but rouse a Greek philosopher from his grave.
Whatever happens, it should be a classic.
